Subject: Q3 portfolio commit cleanup & risk triage

Team —

I'm kicking off a short cleanup for the Q3 renewal slate. Finance wants a slimmed commit list by end-of-week so we can finalize the forecast. Please do the following for your accounts by EOD Thursday (18 Jun):

- Move deals that are not actually committed to "at-risk" (don't leave them in "commit").
- Mark explicit blockers (legal, procurement, budget) in the "notes" field of the sheet.
- For any customer you think is churn-risk, add a single-line rationale and estimated $ at-risk.

Attached is the workbook with the current portfolio view (tab:_commits, tab:_at-risk). I flagged accounts that haven't had a CS touch in 60+ days. Primary asks:

1) Marissa: prioritize the 6 Enterprise renewals (Acme, Solara, BlueFinn, etc.) — note any procurement hold-ups.
2) Ben: please validate ARR numbers for accounts you own and add any late contract terms (extensions, MRR adjustments).
3) Vivek: I'll need a headcount/discount request if you see any revenue we need to protect.

I will collate everything on Friday morning and share an updated forecast with FP&A. If you have objections to moving any specific deals, reply inline.

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

- Solara: Sales expects to push to 9/1; I'll flag as "delayed" rather than at-risk for now.

I'll update the workbook tonight and add short rationales to any at-risk rows.

Looping in some specifics on ACME (RW-EXP-4831) — flagged as at-risk in the sheet and added churn notes. Key points:

- ARR on file: $480k annual. Customer requested a one-time 30% discount for the renewal term citing budget reforecast; finance will not sign off without exec approval.
- Procurement asked for our SOC2 and data-retention policy (I attached the checklist request to the row).
- Sales/CS alignment: CSM warned the customer feels neglected after the last integration hiccup.

I'm attaching a quick CSV of churn observations I aggregated (churn_notes_2026-06.csv). Recommend: set Acme to "at-risk — exec escalation" and propose a 2-week customer success play: executive business review + technical remediation plan.

Ben

Maria —

Following up on behalf of Redwood to ensure we have the right plan for your August renewal. Ben and Marissa have been in the loop; I wanted to confirm whether procurement still needs the SOC2 and retention artifacts, and whether your team expects to proceed with the renewal at the previously discussed terms.

Proposed next steps:
- We can schedule a 30-min EBR this week to run through the integration items and outstanding procurement asks.
- If you prefer, I can loop in our security lead for a short artifact walk-through.

Ben noted a request for a one-time concession. We are open to discussion if there's a clear business justification; I'd like to understand the internal budget timing so we can evaluate options.

Can you confirm availability for a 30-min sync tomorrow or Thursday?

Best,
Logan Wright
